operations.value:
Add a destructive, opt-in compaction/archive protocol for sealed tasks only. Export or preserve provenance, create a parentless checkpoint with a new history generation and compactedFrom pointer, coordinate remote CAS safely, and document that physical Git object cleanup depends on reflogs, refs, remotes, and host retention.

Attachments tie-in (2026-08-13): the comments/attachments story (WB-01KYD77EV9XVA1K0KBY2561GGC) stores file blobs reachable ONLY through their own task's ref history — no shared store, no cross-task dedup — precisely so compaction can reclaim them. The compaction verb should therefore offer a per-task choice: --keep-attachments (copy live attachment blobs into the parentless checkpoint's tree; history reclaimed, current attachments survive) or --strip-attachments (drop the blobs, leave tombstone metadata: name, size, hash, removed-by-compaction). Attachments removed before compaction reclaim automatically either way, since nothing references them. Recompression is not worth building — images are already compressed and git zlib-compresses text; keep-vs-strip is the whole dial.
